Advantages: Readily available around the clock in most centres
Strong validation in prospective management/outcome studies
May provide alternative diagnosis if PE excluded
Disadvantages: Exposure to iodine contrast: limited use in iodine allergy and hyperthyroidism
Risks with iodinated contrast in pregnant and breastfeeding women
Contraindicated in severe renal failure (due to contrast)
Tendency to overuse because of easy accessibility
Clinical relevance of CTPA diagnosis of subsegmental PE unknown
CTPA.Radiation: Effective dose approximately 3–10 mSv (note: significant radiation exposure to young female breast tissue)

Advantages: Strong validation in prospective management/outcome studies
Disadvantages: Not readily available in all centres
Cannot provide alternative diagnosis if PE excluded
Planar V/Q scan.Radiation: Lower radiation than CTPA; effective dose approximately 1–2 mSv

Advantages: High accuracy according to available data
Disadvantages: Cannot provide alternative diagnosis if PE excluded
No validation in prospective management/outcome studies
V/Q SPECT.Radiation: Lower radiation than CTPA; effective dose approximately 1–2 mSv

General notes: Table compares imaging modalities for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE): CTPA, planar V/Q scan, V/Q SPECT
